Session-based recommendation aims to predict the next item in a user interaction sequence, a field where neural networks have recently shown superior performance over other approaches. However, existing high-performing session recommendations often fail to account for the transient nature of user sessions, which are typically brief and limited to just a few item interactions. This study introduces an innovative self-guided graph training method to enhance session-oriented recommendation systems. By constructing a high-order, self-guided item co-dependency graph, the model facilitates more effective feature extraction from short activity periods. Furthermore, the proposed Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) utilizes edge weights representing the significance of high-order relationships to prioritize connections, thereby improving recommendation accuracy for brief sessions. Empirical results across three real-world datasets demonstrate that this method surpasses current state-of-the-art session-oriented recommendation techniques.

This paper defines group $n$-th root (or LCM) codes and group reversible $n$-th root (or LCM) codes on an abelian group. We provide characterizations of these group $n$-th root (or LCM) codes as well as their group reversible $n$-th root (or LCM) codes. Additionally, we demonstrate that a group $n$-th root (or LCM) code is group reversible $n$-th root (or LCM) code if and only if its projection onto the quotient of the code by its kernel forms a direct product of the quotient of the code by its intersection with its center and the quotient of the code by its intersection with its center. We also give examples of these group $n$-th root (or LCM) codes.

We establish a general framework for assigning values to Feynman diagrams invariantly and differentially, applicable to diagrams of arbitrary complexity. This approach relies on a combinatorial complex associated with the diagrams, on which we define differential shapes. Furthermore, we construct a differential equation whose solution yields integral evaluations for these diagrams, a method that generalizes the application of Picard-Fuchs equations. As a side benefit, this work provides a fresh perspective on applying Feynman integrals within topological recursion and mirror symmetry.

Although object recognition involves extracting a hierarchy of features ranging from basic visual elements to complex attributes, it remains unclear how recurrent neural networks (RNNs) manage the flow of this hierarchical data during categorization. This research investigates feature dynamics within the recurrent layers of object classification RNNs. We discovered that early on, category-unrelated, orthogonal features dominate, followed by a rapid transition to a state dominated by category-relevant information. These underlying patterns are largely determined by the network's weight initialization strategy. Furthermore, these pre-categorization, category-orthogonal features facilitate efficient processing by partitioning the input space into linearly separable subregions aligned with fundamental object attributes, thereby reducing complex tasks into simpler categorization steps. Ultimately, these findings indicate that trained RNNs utilize hierarchical feature organization to break down object recognition into a sequence of manageable subtasks.

This work examines how interactions affect a one-dimensional lattice model featuring both non-Hermitian skin effects and topology defined by point gaps. We reveal that while weak interactions preserve the system's non-Hermitian topological status—as verified by a modified bulk invariant—strong interactions cause this skin-topology connection to break. We provide a theoretical framework based on a generalized bulk invariant to explain the origins of this phenomenon. Furthermore, we demonstrate that spatially separating bulk modes, characteristic of the non-Hermitian skin effect, are no longer possible when the point gap is diminished due to strong interactions.

This paper addresses designs of polyphase Golay complementary structures. We introduce a general method for constructing the complement of a composite sequence by combining the compleayles of its constituent parts, thereby linking polyphase Golay complementary structures with inverse autocorrelation. Using these concepts, we introduce two specific methods: the first establishes a pathway to create the complement of a sequence formed by multiplying a unimodular sequence with an arbitrary sequence, while the second generates the complement of a sequence formed by multiplying a unimodular sequence with an arbitrary sequence. Finally, we illustrate our findings with several examples.

This work presents the projected sensitivity of the CMS experiment to the width of the Higgs boson ($\Gamma_H$) and its di-photon ($HH \to 4\ell$) and di-lepton ($HH \to 2\ell 2\nu$) couplings, utilizing on-shell and off-shell production mechanisms. The analysis leverages CMS data collected at $\sqrt{s} = 13$~TeV with an integrated luminosity of 35~fb$^{-1}$. The study concentrates on the region of the Higgs invariant mass ($m_{4\ell}$) exceeding 220~GeV, where the differential cross section is dominated by off-shell production. The methodology relies on the shape of the $m_{4\ell}$ distribution, which is sensitive to the di-photon ($HH \to 2\gamma 2\gamma$) and di-lepton ($HH \to 2\ell 2\gamma$) couplings, as well as the Higgs width ($\Gamma_H$) and off-shell production rates. The presented projections are based on a template fitting approach that incorporates the most significant theoretical and experimental uncertainties.

Deep learning has recently transformed the field of change detection in hyperspectral images. While many current approaches depend heavily on extensive annotated datasets, which are difficult and costly to acquire for these complex scenarios, this study introduces an unsupervised algorithm that requires no labeled data. We propose a deep autoencoder architecture that combines two distinct convolutional depth layers, each utilizing different kernels to effectively capture alterations at both fine and broad scales. By integrating features from these varying perspectives, the model enhances detection sensitivity to changes of various sizes. Furthermore, we developed a novel metric based on the Euclidean distance within latent space to quantify differences between encoded representations. Comprehensive experiments conducted on the HYPERION dataset demonstrate that this method surpasses existing techniques, yielding superior performance.

The integers $0, 1, \ldots, 24$ are partitioned into four disjoint sets $\{A_0, A_1, A_2, A_3\}$, where each $A_i$ contains eight elements, such that the sets of squares of elements in each $A_i$ are pairwise non-intersecting. We demonstrate that if $\sum_{n \in A_i} n = S_i$ for each $i \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, then the quotient ratios $\frac{S_1}{S_0}$, $\frac{S_2}{S_1}$, and $\frac{S_3}{S_2}$ cannot all equal the same value.

In this paper, we present an analysis of spin and valley interactions within silicon structures, ranging from nanometer to atomic scales. Our findings reveal that individual molecules situated on the Si(001) surface can transfer spin information between Si valence bands via interactions with adsorbates possessing unpaired electrons, such as hydrogen. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this effect can be observed and utilized at the nano level by employing a scanning tunneling microscope functioning as a localized electrical probe.

Optimization methods are widely used to solve problems across various domains, though their development remains challenging. To address this, we introduce LibOPT, an open-source Python framework that unifies a broad spectrum of existing and novel optimization algorithms under a consistent interface. LibOPT features a robust set of tools for comparing methods on standard benchmarks, analyzing performance, and visualizing outcomes, all of which facilitate the creation of visualizations and comparative analyses that would otherwise be difficult to produce. Furthermore, the library includes a specialized sub-component for quickly prototyping new algorithms, allowing innovative methods to be registered and tested immediately without extensive refactoring. By streamlining experimentation, LibOPT enables researchers to dedicate more research time to formulating innovative concepts rather than investing effort in basic comparison and analysis workflows.

This paper introduces the notion of a uniform $K$-algebraic variety along with associated concepts such as subvariation, quotient variation, and transfer of morphisms, subsequently examining uniform affine and projective varieties within the framework of these ideas. We further define the transfer of polynomial functions and introduce a metric termed the "transfer degree" to evaluate how much information is retained during transfer. Key results establish a precise relationship between the transfer degrees of functions before and after morphisms, thereby generalizing the classical Lagrange interpolation theorem. As direct applications of these findings, we derive a $K$-algebraic version of the Noether Normalization Lemma and a complete characterization of when uniform algebraic varieties embed directly into $\mathbb{A}_k^n$.

In non-commutative spacetimes, the coordinates undergo a deformation that alters the nature of quantum entities, specifically changing their spin and parity based on their momentum. While this deformation holds significant promise for addressing long-standing problems in high-energy physics, it introduces a critical flaw: fundamental conservation laws, including those for parity, become violated during processes involving particles. This paper investigates how such conservation violations manifest within the framework of the Moyal plane to determine if they can be avoided through a specific transformation of the particle operators. An exploration of alternative operator transformations further reveals that even these alternatives result in an excess of degrees of freedom. Ultimately, it appears impossible to retain both the desirable non-local deformation and the necessary conservation laws simultaneously.

Synthetic single-crystalline diamond is a promising candidate for advanced applications in electronics and sensing due to its exceptional thermal conductivity, wide bandgap, and high charge-carrier saturation velocity. However, the fundamental charge conduction mechanisms within this material remain insufficiently understood. This study introduces a novel Two-Photon Absorption Boundary Transient-Current (TPABTC) method utilizing ultrafast pulsed lasers to map charge current flows in synthetic single-crystalline diamond. By employing this technique, we visualized and quantified ultrafast three-dimensional charge current maps, revealing the anisotropic carrier current properties across the various crystallographic planes of the diamond structure. Furthermore, we measured carrier saturation velocities along all crystallographic directions, providing direct experimental evidence that supports the theoretical predictions of anisotropic saturation currents.

The rise of online hate speech has prompted significant interest in developing specialized detection tools. However, identifying hate speech—particularly within the context of Arabic, which is underrepresented in current research—remains a major challenge. Additionally, merely flagging such content is insufficient; understanding the specific nuances of the hate expressed is crucial for effective moderation. To address these gaps, this study introduces a dual-objective framework: first, building robust models to detect hate speech in the Arabic language, and second, introducing multi-task learning approaches to classify the type of hate speech, thereby offering deeper insight.

This paper examines fractional backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) of delayed type with postponed generator (PO-GBDEs) involving partial derivatives in the Caputo sense with respect to time in the range $0 < \alpha \le 1$. Initially, we establish the existence and uniqueness of a unique solution for these equations under Lipschitz-type conditions on the coefficients. Following this, assuming a stronger condition of monotonicity on the generator, our final results demonstrate the dependence of solutions on $\xi$, $f$, and their associated parameters, quantifying these variations through specific bounds.

Existing approaches to model-based reinforcement learning primarily focus on optimizing long-term rewards, often neglecting the critical need for resilience against disturbances and attacks. This study addresses this gap by introducing a formal framework that simultaneously optimizes a task-specific reward and a risk-aversion metric to generate robust policies. We adapt the information-theoretic mutual information between a system's state and the current policy to quantify and optimize system health, thereby enhancing resilience. To enable long-horizon policy learning, we employ vectorized system models to accelerate the proposed method, which we name Stochastic Model-Driven Policy (SMDP). We validate the SMDP algorithm across two distinct scenarios: a linear system navigating obstacles and a nonlinear system tasked with stable flight maneuvers despite disturbances and cyber intrusions. Empirical results demonstrate that SMDP outperforms current state-of-the-art model-based methods by yielding more resilient policies, a finding further corroborated by tests using a cyber-physical drone environment.

We introduce a novel framework for caching-assisted distributed storage that unifies existing results and facilitates new findings. First, we demonstrate a general method to transform any encoded caching scheme into a decentralized computation protocol. Subsequently, we show how decentralized computation protocols can be converted into encoded caching schemes, establishing a specific tradeoff between file recovery bandwidth and encoded caching storage. Finally, we present a broad class of computation-driven encoded caching schemes that achieve optimality within this tradeoff according to the stated conjectures.

Under the univalent types hypothesis, univalent semantics for a subset of Plotkin's Concurrent Recursive Functions (PCF) can be developed within the framework of univalent mathematics (Wu, 2019). In this paper, we present univalent semantics for an extended version of PCF that includes constructs for equality types and truncated higher inductive types. This extended framework enables a distinct separation between the lower and upper adjoints, providing a foundation for comprehending and defining continuous functions within PCF.

This paper investigates the pole elimination process of Eisenstein series for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ and reveals that the resulting regularized expressions retain significant arithmetic meaning. Specifically, these terms can be decomposed into a sum of Whittier-Wallach type contributions and certain special mass terms. The computation of these individual components relies heavily on intricate combinatorics; in the $GL(2,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ case, this involves the combinatorics of binary trees, whereas for $GL(n,\mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q})$ with $n>2$, it involves the combinatorics of Dyck paths.

This paper introduces a novel configuration-aware secure control strategy for mobile manipulators, ensuring secure trajectories by leveraging Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) and accounting for system nonlinearities. Secure trajectories are defined as paths that evade hazards within an obstacle avoidance region while maintaining satisfaction of system equality constraints. To achieve this, a new configuration-savvy secure control framework is proposed, which reformulates the hazards avoidance problem into a second-order cone program (SOCP). This approach offers significant advantages over existing CBF-based control methods by ensuring fast solution times suitable for real-time deployment and enhanced trajectory smoothness. Experimental results validate the efficacy of this proposed framework.

Natural language processing (NLP) has seen significant advancements in recent years, with text summarization emerging as a critical area of research. This study presents an extractive approach to summarization that utilizes both words and sentences as fundamental units. The proposed method constructs a sentence graph where each node represents a sentence, and edges denote the presence of shared words; these edges are assigned a weight proportional to the frequency of those words. We then apply the betweenness centrality algorithm to calculate the importance of each sentence within this network. By ranking sentences based on this metric, the most significant ones are selected to generate the final summary.

We introduce a framework to derive and analyze nonlinear, non-hermitian, single-mode bosonic operators that modify the conventional definitions of the annihilation, creation, and number operators ($a$, $a^\dagger$, and $a^\dagger a$, respectively). This study is motivated by the fact that recent works have shown these engineered nonlinear quantum systems can be precisely mapped to the Gross-Pitaevskii equation describing a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) featuring contact nonlinearities of both $\lambda$ and $\lambda^2 + \lambda'^{*}$ types, specifically the $\lambda c + \lambda^{*} d^{\dagger}$ type mentioned in the prompt. Specifically, we demonstrate that applying these operators to a coherent state $| \alpha |$ yields a mean-field expectation value identical to the Gross-Pitaevskii wavefunction for a BEC contained in a harmonic trap. Although these operators lack hermiticity, they preserve coherence among their eigenstates, enabling the construction of an unusual set of nonlinear Fock states $| n |$ with $n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$.

This paper proves that five distinct non-degenerate meromorphic maps from a complete Calabi-Yau (or more precisely, a complete K\"{a}hler) manifold $M$ whose general position target varieties are not allowed to share four hyperplanes have a minimum of $n+2$ shared common values, where $n$ denotes the dimension of $M$.

Determining the nondegenerate region for polynomial equation systems is crucial for symbolic computation, yet current methods typically rely on computing the complete discriminant calculus (CDC), a task that is both complex and computationally expensive. This paper introduces a more efficient approach that avoids calculating the full CDC. The core strategy involves using the subresultant polynomial sequence to locate potential nondegenerate zones and a signature-oriented method to verify these regions. Specifically, the signature of the first few elements within the normalized subresultant sequence distinguries cases of real root count changes. By employing root isolation techniques to pinpoint intervals where the root count varies, the method locates zeros of candidate polynomials, thereby identifying the nondegenerate region. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing techniques.

The evaluation of low-momentum photons serves as a critical tool for distinguishing between hadronic processes and hard scattering events. This study introduces a novel methodology for calculating the background contribution to the photon pair spectrum, specifically targeting the region of transverse momentum $k_{\perp} < 0.15$ GeV/c observed in Au+Au collisions. This technique has been extended to analyze photons from Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}=200$ GeV. While the direct comparison between photon spectra from Cu+Cu and two-nucleon emission references offers limited insight, our background-focused approach yields significant results. Specifically, we observe a pronounced enhancement in the $p/\gamma$ excess in Cu+Cu interactions relative to expectations derived from an additive model based on these references.

This paper addresses Turán's "challenging" (or "arduous") tetrahedron problem, which seeks the largest subset of integer lattice points in the $n$-dimensional unit cube $[0,1]^n$ that avoids containing any degenerate tetrahedron. We establish an upper bound of $O(n^{2d/4+d/2})$ for the case where $d \ge 2$, improving upon the previous best limit of $O(n^{2d/4+3d/4})$. Consequently, we prove that for dimensions $d \ge 2$, the expected count of degenerate tetrahedrons in a random subset of size $kn^d$ decays exponentially fast when $k$ falls below a specific threshold. Furthermore, our findings regarding the $\ell_2$-metric extend to the $\ell_1$-metric, yielding an exponential drop in degeneracy for random subsets of size $kn^d$ of dimension $d$ in $\ell_1$. These advances build upon previous work by Alon, Shparlinski, and others, who showed an exponential drop for subsets of size $kn^d$ in $\ell_1$. Our approach combines classical combinatorial techniques with modern tools from probability theory and harmonic analysis.

When rendering thin lines on vector maps at low resolutions, vector anti-aliasing techniques are essential for generating visually pleasing results. This study examines the effective anti-aliasing of line connections between map features, a process vital for both aesthetic quality and visual accuracy. We introduce a straightforward yet potent algorithm that determines the precise maximum thickness required to render these connecting lines free from aliasing artifacts. Furthermore, we evaluate this approach against two traditional alternatives: one relying on pixel sampling and the other on ray marching. Experimental outcomes demonstrate that this spatially effective method performs equally well in speed while surpassing these spatial anti-aliasing alternatives in efficiency.

Recent developments in quasi-interpolation for radial basis function (RBF) schemes have focused on preserving positive, constant, and linear functions. However, maintaining these properties using conditionally positive definite RBFs remains challenging. In this paper, a new RRB family is introduced that possesses conditionally positive definite attributes while retaining the capacity to exactly represent constants and linear functions. Leveraging this novel RBF scheme, a quasi-interpolation operator is constructed capable of exact reproduction of constant and linear functions. Numerical experiments confirm both the high precision of this method and its superior performance.

This study presents a new catalog containing 111 gamma-ray shells associated with pulsar wind bubbles and shells in the Milky Way. In the rapidly evolving landscape of climate science, the availability of extensive image datasets is crucial for advancing research. This paper introduces Climate-Cat, a new multi-class dataset comprising 10 distinct categories of natural landscapes and weather conditions, totaling over 10,000 labeled images. To ensure robust evaluation, the dataset was split into three distinct test sets that are mutually exclusive, as well as two sets for validation and training purposes. We further developed a comprehensive image augmentation strategy to address potential class imbalances and variations in set sizes. Our work presents thorough assessments of various Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures, including an analysis of their performance differences, a study on the impact of input image resolution, and an evaluation of the impact of multiple test augmentations. Finally, we offer in-depth insights into the experimental results to guide future researchers working with this dataset.

This study examines how organizations, economic factors, and research influence one another regarding climate change. Specifically, it analyzes the structural interplay between a research sector and an active sector of 'green' organizations, showing that this mutual relationship drives research activity. Furthermore, it demonstrates that this sector of green organizations exerts a positive influence on the real economy, with the subsequent acceleration of research also benefiting the economy. Using an extended version of the Solow model, the paper shows that this combined interaction of organization, economics, and research results in a permanent elevation of the economy, while the respective roles of green organizations and research push the growth trajectory upward.

Soft grippers offer significant advantages over rigid counterparts, including multi-finger versatility, high dexterity, and superior force distribution, yet their complex nonlinear dynamics pose challenges for precise force and displacement control, which is critical for manipulating delicate objects. While the traditional Koopman operator framework has enhanced modeling and control across various engineering domains, its application to soft multi-fingered grippers remains unexplored. This study introduces a novel virtual modeling and regulation strategy for soft multi-fingered grippers by integrating the Koopman operator method with system theory. Initially, a discrete-time Koopman model is constructed by mapping nonlinear dynamics into a linear operator space. Subsequently, a linear regulator is designed based on these infinite-dimensional linear representations to ensure stable behavior. Finally, experimental results validate both the accuracy of the proposed virtual models and their efficacy for reliable force control.

In 2018, Zhang and Sato introduced a discrete optimization technique designed to find global solutions for non-convex polynomial minimization problems. This original method operates within a discrete framework, where the solution set is restricted to Gaussian-Hermite quadrature points of varying orders, creating distinct yet overlapping search spaces at each iteration. This design presents significant challenges: determining the optimal order for these iterative search spaces and mitigating performance degradation caused by the lack of a unified search space. To resolve these issues, we introduce a continuous variant of Zhang and Sato's method. Furthermore, we adapt the framework to organic forms, resulting in the development of "Organic Gradient Descent."

We report the discovery of a new radio source, J2102+6015, identified through a search of the VLA Ultra-Deep Survey (UDS) data. This object exhibits a flux density of 1.01 ± 0.04 μJy at 1.4 GHz and was subsequently observed using the MeerKAT radio telescope, yielding a measurement of 1.03 ± 0.04 μJy at 1.6 GHz. Our analysis indicates that J2102+6015 is a new radio counterpart at a redshift of z = 4.575 ± 0.002, which is the most distant radio source detected to date. This source is spatially associated with the previously unidentified galaxy candidate at z = 4.578 ± 0.002 (Kim et al. 2019). Furthermore, its radio luminosity of 1.7 × 10⁸ L⊙_1.4GHz places it among the most luminous radio sources found in the early universe. Given its weak radio emission, we hypothesize that this signal originates from a youthful, young starburst event.

Non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) is a prevalent and deadly malignancy that remains difficult to diagnose and treat. Although CT scans are the standard for assessing this disease, they suffer from low contrast, resulting in poor visual quality for images. We introduce a new multimodal educational dataset designed to support NSCLC prediction research. This collection integrates low-contrast CT scan data with patient records, including age, gender, and smoking history. To enhance the dataset, we developed a synthetic augmentation technique that simulates various smoking scenarios. Furthermore, we created a comprehensive annotation system featuring expert radiologist reports and derived ground-truth labels. To validate our approach, we applied state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, specifically Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, for multi-modal classification tasks. Our experimental outcomes demonstrate that our proposed methodology is viable and holds significant promise for future clinical applications.

In recent years, various state representation methods for describing the natural language environment have been proposed within language-based reinforcement learning. However, a unified summary of these approaches is currently missing. This work systematically categorizes and compares existing state representation techniques according to the grammatical structure of natural language. Furthermore, we address several under-researched areas and propose potential future investigation paths for these problems.

We propose a novel method for reconstructing the matter power spectrum from individual quasar spectra. Using the random forest machine learning algorithm, we successfully generate accurate estimates of the linear matter density contrast, $\delta_{\rm lin}$, directly from high-resolution high-redshift quasar spectra. By applying Gaussian smoothing to these estimates, we derive the power spectrum, $P(k)$, achieving high fidelity with minimal computational cost. We tested our approach using the BOSS CMASS sample, constructing the power spectrum independently at every data point and subsequently validating it against standard post-processing techniques. Our results demonstrate that this individual-spectrum reconstruction method matches the precision of traditional methods that rely on pre-computed $\delta_{\rm lin}$ fields. Furthermore, the computational efficiency of our technique renders it a powerful tool for real-time analysis during future large-scale surveys.

Weyl modules, which serve as universal highest-weight modules, constitute the fundamental class of modules for the polynomial algebra $\mathbb C[x]$. This article extends this definition to broader families of operators dominated by Lie algebras of derivation operators. Consequently, we define a corresponding class of modules termed "almost Weyl modules." We demonstrate that both Weyl and these so-called almost Weyl modules constitute universal highest-weight modules within their respective categories. Furthermore, we establish criteria identifying when such modules are irreducible and provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of unique highest-weight vectors, along with an alternative definition for irreducibility in this framework. Our findings also establish a duality relationship between Weyl and almost Weyl modules. Ultimately, we derive conditions under which these modules are $U(\frak h)$-excluded, where $\mathfrak h$ denotes the Lie algebra governing harmonic polynomials.

Sentiment analysis stands as a vital component of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and has been extensively studied over the years. Although traditional methods often struggle with the nuances of Social Media Sentiment Analysis (SOTA), these challenges have driven researchers toward machine learning algorithms, which have recently shown superior results compared to earlier techniques. This paper introduces an Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework designed to evaluate Twitter sentiment, leveraging recent advancements in neural networks. We present an efficient approach to generate sentence-level binary labels for tweets, utilizing multi-layer graph visualizations to interpret the trained model and enhance its transparency.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently achieved remarkable success across various natural language processing tasks. This paper introduces ConverseGPT, an LLM-driven, role-defined dialogue system built on the GPT-3 architecture, which is optimized for specific conversation tasks through a three-stage framework: data preparation, model fine-tuning, and ensemble generation. During data preparation, we build a specialized corpus by aggregating publicly available language and curating relevant dialogue datasets. In fine-tuning, LLMs are adjusted for a specific conversation task using our compiled data. Finally, the generation phase employs an ensemble of fine-tuned models to produce high-quality responses. Evaluated across three different dialogue benchmarks, our method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques. Additionally, to broaden the application scope, this work presents an open-source application programming interface (API) for the community.

"Remnant gravitational wave memory" refers to the distinct, non-linear component of gravitational wave radiation that persists even as the standard, non-linear "prompt" waves fade away. In this paper, we investigate whether a stochastic background formed by these remnant waves could be detected by future-generation interferometers. Our findings indicate that signals arising from sources such as binary neutron star mergers are orders of magnitude too weak for current detection capabilities. Conversely, when these remnant waves combine over cosmological distances, their potential strength increases significantly. We propose a new theoretical framework to quantify these cumulative effects, estimating a non-linear contribution roughly $10^4$ times stronger than the linear one. Although detectable in principle, this hypothetical background would be completely masked by the established stochastic noise generated from binary black hole mergers.

We introduce a model wherein supersymmetry is broken via a phase transition in the scalar sector of the gravitino, facilitated by the interaction between a complex SUSY-breaking spurion superfield $X$ and a gauge-singlet scalar field $S$. The scalar component of $X$ acquires its vacuum expectation value during the electroweak phase transition, whereas the phase of $X$'s vacuum expectation value evolves dynamically. During the SUSY-breaking phase transition, the scalar field $S$ can become trapped in a metastable minimum, forming a dark hole that gravitationally decays into high-energy particles. Specifically, we investigate a scenario where dark holes form in the energy range of $10^{15}$ GeV. Within this framework, we examine the cosmological implications regarding the abundance of dark matter, the generation of a stochastic gravitational wave background, and the generation of leptons.

To enable agents to learn shared semantics through practice, this work introduces an integrative neuro-symbolic signaling framework. It combines a symbolic learner equipped with domain knowledge and a neural neural network, with both components exchanging information via bidirectional communication. This architecture facilitates the bidirectional exchange between symbolic and neural components, supported by a causal intervention mechanism. Specifically, the symbolic element deduces the identities of underlying objects by analyzing the behaviors of the neural network, while the neural network acquires robustness against variability by filtering out irrelevant symbols based on the causal structure of knowledge provided by the symbolic partner. Consequently, this model generates signaling systems that are both anti-fragile and efficient, achieving robust data compression.

Forecasting specific terms within evolving languages is a critical task with widespread utility across numerous domains. This study introduces a new hybrid architecture for predicting emerging words, which integrates the Naive Bayes algorithm with results derived from latent data. To effectively identify terms with sparse occurrences, we leverage a probabilistic term representation derived via latent semantic analysis. Concurrently, we employ Naive Bayes to process this latent information, a decision grounded in its capacity to function with minimal assumptions and small datasets. This dual approach harnesses both first-layer data characteristics and second-layer latent structures, yielding a novel hybrid solution. Experimental evaluations across three real-world datasets demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, exhibiting significantly higher accuracy in predicting forecast terms.

We introduce a new recommendation task called Phase-Smartened Guidance (PSEG), designed to enhance user experience by providing two types of suggestions: session-level and phase-level. Session-level guidance offers a prioritized list of items, whereas phase-level guidance recommends the specific suggestion stage within a session where the user should take the next action. To tackle PSEG, we developed a two-phase Suggestion Framework (TPEG). The first phase generates session suggestions using a graph neural network (GNN)-based user session representation, while the second phase handles in-session guidance by employing a two-stage model to identify guidance phases and predict the next item. Additionally, we established a novel dataset, Two-Phase Advice Collection (TPAC), which contains both session and phase recommendations alongside item interactions from Amazon. Experimental results demonstrate that TPEG significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models on both tasks. Specifically, TPEG surpasses session-only suggestion methods by 10.8% in Hit Ratio@20 (HR@20) and 2-phase advice generation models by 14.4% HR@20. Finally, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each proposed component.

Active particles, such as colloids driven by internal fuel consumption, exhibit unique self-propelled dynamics that diverge significantly from passive Brownian motion. This work investigates active colloidal systems subjected to spatially modulated propulsion speeds, exploring how external gradients influence particle behavior. We derive a coarse-grained framework that captures particle accumulation and orientation statistics, revealing that while position-specific propulsion speeds create macroscopic current patterns, they do not alter the underlying hydrodynamic dispersion coefficient. Consequently, active mixing arises from the interplay between these propulsion variations and active advection. Furthermore, we demonstrate that particle orientation becomes decorrelated on timescales set by either the advection coefficient or the inverse of the propulsion decay time. These theoretical predictions are substantiated by extensive molecular dynamics simulations, which align closely with our analytical models.

Discrete fracture network (DFN) models are increasingly favored for simulating fluid transport in fractured rocks because they offer high geometric fidelity and the computational flexibility to handle complex fracture systems. Within these networks, fractures are represented as discrete elements of specific dimensions, connected at nodes representing their intersections. A central challenge in DFN modeling is the development of robust numerical schemes that accurately capture fluid movement across fractures and ensure continuous pressure and flux at their intersections. This paper introduces a new three-dimensional mimetic finite element method designed for DFNs that leverages an original network construction approach. The proposed framework is built upon a network that spans the entire DFN and is built from a set of local meshes surrounding each fracture segment. These local meshes are created by placing control volumes on both sides of the segment and connecting them. A unique feature of this method is its ability to define a global network specifically tailored to the geometry of DFNs, which enables the application of advanced three-dimensional mimetic finite element techniques. This approach yields a mathematical formulation that is both conservative and physically consistent, effectively modeling three-dimensional fluid flow.

This study addresses challenges related to collision avoidance and structural preservation within drone point sets. We introduce two innovative solutions: the new collision-free algorithm (NCPA) and the cellular formation maintenance (CFM). Under standard assumptions of perfect sensor accuracy and unlimited computational power, the NCPA algorithm aligns the current drone formation with a predefined reference pattern by minimizing distance metrics between corresponding points. Meanwhile, the CFM guides each aircraft toward a target reference position defined by its sector's centroid. The NCPA operates on pairwise interactions, whereas the CFM relies on sector-level dynamics. The NCPA ensures constant inter-drone spacing, while the CFM sustains formation geometry. The combined approach offers significant advantages, including robustness to sensor inaccuracies and computational constraints, along with enhanced structure retention and safety margins.

Let $G$ be a connected graph possessing an $n$-vertex count and a Seidel matrix denoted by $S(G)$. The range, denoted as $R(G)$, is defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum values found in the spectrum of $S(G)$. This study establishes a specific condition under which $R(G)$ equals $n-1$, simultaneously providing several cases where the range is $n$ or $n+1$. Furthermore, the energy associated with $G$ and its Seidel matrix $S(G)$ is also examined.

This study explores optimal management under uncertainty, modeled by the stochastic differential equation. The research is distinguished by two key features: the inclusion of retrospective integrals and the driver's dependence on fractional Brownian motion. To address this, the paper first establishes the uniqueness and continuous dependence of solutions. Subsequently, it derives the corresponding quasi-variation derivatives and first-order conditions. Finally, it presents sufficient conditions for optimality within a two-agent framework.

This study investigates elliptic finite-band solutions for a non-self-adjoint Dirac equation involving two five by five matrices, one of which is Hermitian and the other is arbitrary. The canonical form of the associated Lax operator is derived, and its spectral characteristics are examined. Additionally, the study presents explicit examples of such solutions alongside their corresponding abelian differential quotients. It is further demonstrated that these elliptic solutions converge to the soliton solutions observed in a self-adjoint Dirac operator featuring a specific potential.

This study introduces a two-tier heterogeneous Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET) architecture comprising RSU-assisted unicast links and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) multihop connections. The primary research goal is to evaluate the end-to-end (e2e) throughput of these dual modes. To achieve this, the authors develop a novel analytical framework that characterizes the multihop network by modeling the spatial distribution of intermediate relays using a thinned Poisson Point Process (PPP). Leveraging this new model, the paper derives the Probability Density Function (PDF) of the number of hops required for transmission. Subsequently, the mean number of multihop links, the $k$-th hop success probability, and the final throughputs for both unicast and multihop communications are rigorously examined. The findings are validated through simulations, with results aligning closely with our new analytical predictions.

Although Wikipedia is renowned for its high-quality, freely accessible encyclopedic content, a significant portion of its article material remains inaccurate or subpar. Identifying such low-quality material is essential to maintain article standards, yet current manual oversight mechanisms are insufficient to effectively monitor the vast influx of edits. This study examines the patterns inherent in contributor editing behaviors to develop a novel framework for automatically tagging wiki material with quality indicators. By leveraging these editorial patterns, we develop a method that performs comparably to, and in some cases surpasses, state-of-the-art natural language processing (NLP) techniques. This approach offers a more efficient solution for quality identification, thereby reducing the burden on volunteer moderators.

This study addresses knowledge transfer in scenarios where a decision-theoretic black box, devoid of access to its internal mechanisms, must have its policy replicated by a transparent agent with full self-awareness. We introduce a decision-making framework utilizing zero-shot knowledge transfer to replicate policies in such black-box agents without internal transparency, contrasting this with decision-by-observation approaches where the visible agent monitors and emulates a black-box system step-by-step. Our methodology, decision theoretic zero-shot knowledge transfer (DT-ZKT), enables a visible agent to emulate a black-box decision-maker by aligning their actions based on shared environmental outcomes rather than direct observation, effectively achieving policy replication through result equivalence instead of stepwise imitation.

A study into the semileeptive decays of $B^0_s$ mesons into final states containing a strange kaon and a charmonium hadron is reported, utilizing proton-proton collision data with a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s}=7$ TeV and an integrated luminosity of $1.0\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb detector. The analysis focuses on the un-polarized, neutral $K^0_S$ final state. Decays of the charm sector are specifically addressed for $\bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D}^0 \to \bar{D

"Twisted torus T-duality represents a duality within the realm of twisted torus geometry. In this article, we generalize twisted torus D-duality to encompass the most comprehensive T-duality scenario applicable to twisted torus geometries—specifically geometric twisted torus T-duality. This articular focus extends the discussion to include the classification of topological T-duality applicable to twisted torus structures. The paper demonstrates that all such topological classifications can be integrated into a unified framework known as generalized geometric twisted torus T-duality. The article subsequently examines geometric T-duality within a broader context: that of generalized twisted torus T-duality. The classification of topological T-duality applicable to generalized twisted torus structures is presented as an integral component of this exploration. The study concludes by investigating geometric T-duality from a broader perspective: that of generalized twisted torus T-duality. The classification of topological T-duality applicable to generalized twisted torus structures is presented as an integral component of this exploration."

Current cooperative observation learning models depend heavily on expert-generated demonstration data, which are often difficult or costly to acquire in practical settings. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel agent-centric approach that eschews the need for expert demonstrations entirely. By leveraging internal agent behaviors as collaborative signals, our method enables effective knowledge sharing based on self-generated actions. We evaluate our framework across three standard navigation benchmarks and two real-world simulation tasks. Results demonstrate performance that rivals or exceeds traditional cooperative observation learning methods trained on expert data. Additionally, we provide thorough analyses of critical design elements within our approach.

This study introduces a novel method for calculating the quark momentum distribution $xT$-dependent, denoted as $F_{\text{unpolarized}}^{(2)}(x, Q^2, \eta)$, within the framework of the Functional Approach to Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). This quantity is essential for analyzing data from the JLab Hall C experiment, which conducted an $ep$ elastic scattering measurement involving a transversely polarized proton target. The text reviews the theoretical model and outlines a strategy to extract the parameters of the code from existing quark momentum distribution data. The reliability of the proposed method is confirmed by its ability to replicate predictions made by standard perturbative QCD. Furthermore, the study outlines future research directions.

Hand-object interactions are vital for understanding physical activity, yet current models relying on top-down, single-view images often fail to capture the full range of real-world interactions due to limited viewpoint diversity and object scale variations. This paper introduces HI-Monitor, a system designed to automatically reconstruct entire sequences of hand-object interactions from wild, multi-view wild point cloud series, requiring no training data. By leveraging contact point analysis to track object state and shape, and by fine-tuning an occupancy prediction network on synthesized interaction data, the model achieves precise reconstructions of objects featuring complex geometry. We evaluate our approach using 110 interaction sequences from the HRI-4K dataset, demonstrating superior performance against baseline methods.

A *C*-collection consists of simplices within a crystallographic arrangement of spheres such that every pair is either disjoint or completely one contained in the other. *non*-*crystallographic* collections, which are topologically significant, are defined by the same property but applied to arbitrary collections of spheres. A collection's interleaving number represents the maximum number of simplices forming a chain where each simplex contains the next. In the study of collections of spheres in $\mathbb{R}^3$, a key question asks if every such collection with an interleaving number $k=2$ (for any rank $n$) must necessarily be non-*crystallographic*. This paper demonstrates that for rank $n=4$, the answer is no. Furthermore, it establishes that any "C"-collection of spheres in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with an interleaving number $k=2$ and rank $n=4$ must possess a specific structural form.

This paper introduces an unsupervised, learning-based method to automatically calibrate the depth camera intrinsics and extrinsics relative to a robot base frame, without requiring manual parameter tuning. The proposed solution adjusts unmarked depth camera parameters by employing a learning-based approach that relies solely on depth images, eliminating the need for labeled training data. The system trains on a simulated environment featuring a diverse set of objects and robots to learn a mapping from depth camera parameters to the end-effector position and orientation relative to the robot. Testing was conducted using a real UR5e system integrated with an Intel RealSense D435i, where a LBR 400+ gripper served as the end-effector. Experimental results demonstrate that the automatic calibration module effectively estimates gripper poses, yielding high accuracy and robustness across varying depth camera setups.

This paper addresses treatments disrupted by exposure to neighboring units' treatment status and actions within a regulated setting, analyzing units as part of an ordered sequence. We introduce a K-nearest neighbor (KNN) interference model, a partially directed acyclic graph where each unit connects to K neighboring units on both sides. Under this framework, we propose a two-stage estimation method for the average treatment effect in presence of interference (ATI) specifically for units deprived of treatment due to KNN interference. Our approach first employs an inverse probability weighting technique to adjust for selection bias, followed by the use of local linear regression to enhance estimation precision. We evaluate the proposed estimator through a Monte Carlo simulation and apply it to real-world data concerning the impact of Head Start participation, a program for low-income preschoolers, on subsequent high school graduation rates.

We investigate neutrino production resulting from dark matter annihilation within neutron stars, focusing on scenarios mediated by pseudoscalar particles. In this framework, neutrinos are generated through two primary mechanisms: neutron beta decay following the annihilation of neutrons bound in dark matter bound states, and direct four-fermion interactions facilitated by the exchange of pseudoscalar mediators. We calculate the corresponding contributions to the neutrino luminosity and demonstrate that, in certain parameter regimes, direct emission dominates over emission produced via dark matter bound states. Leveraging these neutrino emission rates, we derive constraints on the associated parameters by examining the thermal evolution of neutron stars, specifically targeting models where direct emission is the primary source of luminosity.

UNIONS is a ground-based survey designed to image approximately 100 square degrees across the U, g, r, and i bands with high spatial resolution (0.35 arcsec) and deep magnitude limits (reaching ~24). This combination of photometric depth and fine spatial sampling makes it uniquely suited for studying cosmic weak lensing. The current work presents a novel pipeline for generating and analyzing shape measurements, which has been tested on a 1.2 deg² region of sky. The resulting galaxy ellipticity estimates align well with those from the DESY Lensing Pipeline, though they exhibit slightly higher dispersion. The average redshift for the UNIONS sample is determined to be 0.31 ± 0.03.

Kronecker-Weyl equidistribution has long been recognized as a cornerstone of modern number theory. Building on recent observations regarding the lack of uniformity in this equidistribution within certain L-functions families, we establish new genres defined by the Kronecker-Weyl framework. We prove that, for each defined genre, equidistribution holds with an error term of $O(\log^2 Q/\log Q)$; this result is significantly sharper than the traditional $O(\log^3 Q)$ bound found in uniform cases. Furthermore, by analyzing the distribution of Hecke eigenvalues associated with newforms in these genres, we derive improved generic Diophantine approximation statements. These findings yield significant advancements in low-genus Diophantine approximation, notably producing the optimal known approximation exponent for quadratic fields and substantially enhancing previous bounds for quartic fields.

We demonstrate that a local complete intersection $V$ over a field $k$ with characteristic zero, which is either rational over $k$ or satisfies the Du Bois property, is Rationally Connected to $k$ precisely when its singular locus has codimension at least three within $X$. Furthermore, for such a local complete intersection $V$ that is rationally smooth and defined over any field $k$, its natural map from the structure sheaf to the sheaf of differentials, $\mathcal{O}_X \to \omega_{\mbox{\footnotesize{DV}}}^1$, remains isomorphism outside a singular locus of codimension at least three on $X$.

The magnetization response of the field-cooled $\mathrm{BaFe}_{2}(\mathrm{AsO}_{3})_{2}$ compound, a layered barium iron arsenate, was examined under varying magnetic fields and temperatures. The observed behavior is modeled as a crossover from 3D to 2D ordering, where the transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{C}}$) decreases as the applied field drops below a critical threshold ($H_{\mathrm{C}}$). This critical field is identified by analyzing the temperature dependence of the initial susceptibility ($\chi_{\mathrm{I}}$) and aligns with the field required to fully saturate magnetization. Furthermore, the temperature evolution of the critical field ($H_{\mathrm{C}}$) displays a crossover from Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) behavior at low temperatures to mean-field characteristics at higher temperatures, suggesting that the magnetization transition can be interpreted as an adjustable BKT crossover.

We propose a theoretical framework where a keV-scale axion-like particle (ALP) acquires mass through coupling to the photon, allowing it to function as a fermion-like shadow matter constituent. Within this scenario, the fermionic partner behaves as a stable, weakly interacting particle capable of accounting for a significant fraction—or entirety—of the universe's dark matter. We establish a theoretical parameter space consistent with all experimental data and present observational strategies to detect this axion-still-neutrino (ASN) show matter. These detection methods include X-ray searches for decay photons, direct detection experiments, cyclotron-emission observations of magnetized neutron stars, and measurements of cosmic axion-still-neutrino radiation.

This work establishes tighter bounds on approximate stabilizer rank for arbitrary quantum states accessed via random circuit sampling, with these bounds scaling loosely logarithmically against the total number of qubits. By integrating two key techniques—decomposing complex wavefunctions into simpler ones and utilizing approximate tensor contractions—we generate an improved general bound. Furthermore, we introduce a refined algorithmic strategy for classical simulation of specific states within the random circuit sampling framework, which directly yields a strengthened upper limit on stabilizer rank for magic states.

This study investigates the equilibrium status of a holographic dark energy (HoDE) system bounded by a Hubble horizon within a Tsallis non-extensive thermodynamic framework and a Complex form of holographic shadow energy. The model incorporates a background of non-extensive Complex form quintessence energy density coupled to a non-extensive non-negative shadow energy density. Initially, the Rayleigh-Serrr stability criteria are examined, followed by an analysis of the equation of state parameter and its derivative to characterize the matter, radiation, and dark energy eras. Subsequently, the enthalpy and internal energy of the system are derived. Finally, the enthalpy-based Tsallis holographic shadow energy (hoSME) equilibrium status is assessed using the Padmanabhan acceleration formula.

The LAMOST Time-Domain Exploration (LTDE) initiative aims to conduct extensive surveys of the sky using LAMOST, specifically utilizing 4888 dual CCD cameras (referred to as "plates") to capture images across 4000 square degrees. This initiative seeks to detect and analyze transient events such as supernovae, variable stars, and asteroids. The first phase of this project involves monitoring 100 selected plates, scheduled for completion by the end of 2021. The second phase will involve imaging 300 additional plates, each with an exposure repeated three times at intervals of one week. The first report covers data from 32 plates located within the Southern Hemisphere, acquired using the K2 bandpass (centered at 420 nm) during the K2 mode operation. The paper details the K2 observational strategy, data processing pipeline, and presents initial findings, including the identification of 1,032,000 new supernovae candidates and the discovery of 1,032,000 individual stars exhibiting significant variability.

This paper introduces TuRaN, a novel true random number generator (TRNG) that leverages inherent noise within SRAM cells. Although SRAM-based TRNGs are well-established, recent research has exposed vulnerabilities to adversarial attacks, potentially allowing attackers to substitute genuine random data with predictable values. To counter this, we propose a new design that ensures authenticity by first verifying the randomness of generated digits; if the source is compromised, those values are discarded. Additionally, TuRaN implements a sophisticated technique of supply voltage underscaling to amplify variations between adjacent memory cells, yielding two distinct benefits: it elevates the entropy of the output and safeguards against side-channel attacks. Our evaluation across various process nodes and SRAM technologies demonstrates that TuRaN achieves genuine true randomness and remains resilient to both side-channel intrusions and adversary injections.

This paper introduces a design methodology for nonvolatile single-electron resistive (S-E-R) devices utilizing molecular junctions. The core concept involves a single-electron resistor formed by a suspended nanoscale wire connecting two single-electron tunneling (SET) islands, where the wire's resistance exceeds the quantum resistance ($R_{Q} = h/e^{2} \approx 25.8$ k$\Omega$). The device operates as a single-electron resistor when biased below the wire's charging energy threshold and functions as a single-electron relay, switching from high to low resistance under higher voltages, thereby enabling data storage and retrieval via wire charge states. The proposed design workflow begins with selecting an appropriate single-electron island material, followed by choosing a molecular wire that exhibits strong covalent bonding to the island and an intrinsically high resistance. To validate the approach, we simulated junctions composed of benzene-doped pentacene islands and various diphenylenediacetylene (DFT-D) wires. These simulations yielded S-E-R devices with quantized charge states, demonstrating clear switching behavior and estimated charge retention times spanning from seconds to years.

We introduce a novel, efficient method for the symbolic evaluation of multi-loop Feynam integrals, leveraging a recent advancement in their causal depiction. This approach is subsequently applied to numerically assess ten distinct multi-loop massless $U(1)$ gauge theory diagram types, which are essential for calculating the quantum corrections to the QED scattering matrix at second order in $\hbar$. The results are expressed as linear combinations of standard Feynman polynomial denominators and polynomials involving the Mandelstam variables.

In the context of one-dimensional two-state quantum strides featuring a Hermitian operator $\tau$ and its adjobe $t = \tau^*$, an extension formula is established for $\tau$-calculus-based Hilbert space $L^2(\mathbb{R})$-valued square integrable functions. This formula applies specifically to eigenfunctions of $\tau$ under the condition that they adhere to a given eigenvalue. The derivation employs a technique analogous to Green's formula, which necessitates incorporating Green-type identities that incorporate boundary values at infinity. The resulting extension formula encompasses various existing formulas found in scattering theory and quantum well models as special cases.

This study explores hybrid star configurations at the intersection of the Sigma-Omega-Rho model and MIT/ NJL formalisms. Initially, we establish baseline results for the pure Sigma-Omega-Rho model, subsequently deriving the hybrid stars that incorporate quark matter described by the MIT bag model. To enhance these results, we further integrate quarks governed by the Chiral Restoration Density (CRD) approach of the NJL model. Finally, we analyze the mass-radius relationships for these hybrid stars and compare them against observational data from neutron stars, concluding that the hybrid configurations described by the MIT model offer a superior fit to neutron star observations when contrasted with the results derived from the sigma-omega-rho system.

We investigate photon scattering within a rapidly or slowly decelerating optomechanical system featuring a $q$-deformation. Our analysis reveals that adjusting the deformation parameter can enhance transparency and boost the gain coefficient. Consequently, radiation can be amplified significantly even in a rapid slowing regime. Additionally, we examine how varying the deformation parameter influences the optical nonlinearity and the system's linear response to power changes.

The double-rotor model, established by Bengtsson and Bonetti, offers a comprehensive framework for describing the spectrum of odd-A nuclei exhibiting K mixing. This research applies the model to the $^{137}$La spectrum, achieving excellent agreement with experimental data. Notably, the analysis identifies two scissors modes within the nuclear collective motion; notably, one of these appears in an "improper" or adverse configuration.

When examining a two-atom-thick epoxide with metal support, the system exhibits a stable metallic state featuring a half-filled $d_{xz/yz}$ band, which generates a magnetic moment of 1 $\mu_B$ per metal ion. In contrast, a three-atom-thick epoxide with metal support displays stability as an insulator in the half-metal regime, exhibiting a half-filled $d_{xz/yz}$ band, which results in a magnetic moment of 1 $\mu_B$ per metal ion.
